help.title: Help
help.lede: How to work in the console: checklists for your roles, the handbook, what each label means, and the keyboard.
help.checklistNote: Ticks are kept in this browser only.

items.secondFactor: Keep your second factor and recovery codes safe.
items.readGuardRails: Read the guard rails no console can switch off.
items.statusLabels: Learn what Live, Demo, Contract, Designed and Proposed mean.
items.secondStaff: Invite a second staff member so approvals can work.
items.launchGates: Walk through the launch checklist with the compliance officer.
items.legal: Make sure every legal document has counsel approval in every language.
items.approvals: Check the approvals page every day.
items.policy: Write the editorial policy and the AI-labelling rules.
items.sources: Review which sources may be used, and how.
items.reviewRules: Set review rules per format and author type.
items.countryBase: Check the country base and record local additions with sources.
items.taxonomy: Shape the taxonomy and release a version.
items.firstSource: Register the first source with its licence, robots and terms checks.
items.caseGrants: Learn how case grants work: scoped, at most 72 hours, approved by a second person.
items.recovery: Handle recovery escalations with evidence and the cooling-off period.
items.noImpersonation: Remember: there is no “log in as”; explain access with reason codes instead.

docs.guardRails: Hub administration and its guard rails

status.live: Implemented end to end with automated tests. Not yet deployed to production anywhere.
status.demo: The screen exists and is tested, but it runs on synthetic data and nothing is saved.
status.contract: The data shapes and rules are frozen as contracts; no storage or screen yet.
status.designed: An accepted design describes it; no code yet.
status.proposed: Designed for the first time and open for review.

mode.fake: A built-in imitation for trying the hub: nothing reaches a real provider.
mode.manual: A person does the work outside the engine, for example a register look-up.
mode.live: A real provider, enabled by a second person after a synthetic test.

hub.definition: One gathering point for a country or a city, with its own staff, settings and launch gates.

node.definition: One installation of the engine; it can host several hubs.

lifecycle.definition: Draft, preparing, soft launch, public, suspended, closing or closed; moving forward needs passed gates and a second person.

elevation.definition: A console session opened after your password and second factor; it ends after inactivity.

secondPerson.definition: A sensitive change is asked by one staff member and approved by another; nobody approves their own request.

digest.definition: A fingerprint of the exact change; an approval binds it, so any later change voids the approval.

killSwitch.definition: Stops a capability at once; one person engages it, releasing needs a second person and an incident note.

launchGate.definition: A condition with evidence that must pass before soft launch or public; there is no waiver.

configVersion.definition: Settings are never edited in place: each change is a version that is activated and later superseded.

demoData.definition: Synthetic, labelled records; never indexed, never federated, purged before soft launch.

caseGrant.definition: The only way staff see private data: scoped to a case, at most 72 hours, approved by a second person, every read logged.

keys.skip: The first Tab reaches “Skip to content”.
keys.order: Then the band, the navigation, the page heading and the content, in that order.
keys.menu: On a phone the sections open from the “Sections” button as a full-height sheet; Escape closes it.
keys.forms: Every change needs a reason; the result is announced and shown as a notification.

identity.title: Identity and territory
identity.lede: Who and where the hub is: names in every hub language, territories, languages, currency and time zone.
identity.name: Name
identity.territoriesNote: Territories describe where the hub works; they are never exclusive, and restricted places are refused at every level.
identity.versionsNote: Saving creates a new configuration version; the active one stays until the new version is activated.

modes.title: System modes
modes.lede: How the hub behaves: lifecycle stage, data, registration, moderation, automation, indexing and maintenance.
modes.blockedBy: Soft launch is blocked by open gates: {items}.
modes.demoRule: Demo data never leaves the hub, is never indexed or federated, and must be purged before soft launch.
modes.humanGates: Decisions that always belong to a person
modes.supervisedNote: Raising a domain to supervised autonomy needs a second person and active spending caps.
modes.violationsFound: The current modes contradict the lifecycle: {items}.

modules.title: Modules
modules.lede: Which product modules are on in this hub, what each builds on, and how far the engine has built it.
modules.disableNote: Switching a module off hides it from participants; existing records stay and come back when it is switched on again.

legal.title: Legal and operator
legal.lede: The operator of the hub and the documents participants accept; a version becomes active only with counsel approval in every hub language.
legal.fakeScreening: fake adapter, not a real screening
legal.nothingToActivate: No version is approved by counsel and waiting for activation.
legal.templatesNote: A new version starts from the engine's templates; counsel reviews it before activation.

residency.title: Residency and sub-processors
residency.lede: Where personal data is stored and processed, and who processes it for the hub.
residency.contradiction: {services} run outside {country}, the residency country. Check whether personal data reaches them.
residency.privateOutside: A sub-processor outside the residency country receives private data; review the egress rules.
residency.subProcessorsNote: Generated from the hub's connections; every connection in this demo is a fake or manual adapter.
residency.newCountryHelp: Two-letter country code, for example US.

country.title: Country base
country.lede: The country facts the hub relies on: the bound country pack or the generic profile, and the hub's local additions.
country.generic: Generic profile: ISO data only; add identifiers, registers and other facts as local additions.
country.sourcesNote: Every fact in a pack cites its source and states how far it is verified.
country.label: Name
country.export: Export the additions as a country-pack change:
country.keyHelp: A stable key, for example US-CA:cslb.
country.candidateNote: A new addition stays a candidate until the compliance officer confirms it with a source.

taxonomy.title: Taxonomy and units
taxonomy.lede: Topics, categories, plan-step categories and units with their names in every hub language, released as versions.
taxonomy.empty: No taxonomy yet. Start with topics and plan-step categories; the engine's open plan-step taxonomy can be imported.
taxonomy.deprecateNote: Deprecating a term that is in use requires mapping it to another term first.
taxonomy.label: Name

launch.title: Launch checklist
launch.lede: What stands between the hub and soft launch or public. Every gate needs evidence; there is no waiver.
launch.noWaiver: No control waives a gate; an invalidated gate blocks like an open one until it is checked again.

gates.two_staff_with_second_factor: Two staff members with a second factor
gates.i18n_complete: Interface complete in every hub language

launch.evidenceHelp: The identifier of the stored evidence, for example ev-counsel-letter-2.
launch.publicBlocked: {count, plural, one {# gate still blocks going public.} other {# gates still block going public.}}

setup.title: Setup
setup.resume: Your answers are stored on the server, so you can stop and resume with the same link. In this demo nothing is stored.

check.title: Install check
check.purpose: The engine checks the address, database, object storage, worker, clock and secret store before anything else.

help.address: Set the public address to HTTPS (or localhost for a trial).
help.database: Run the migrations; the runtime role must not bypass row-level security.
help.object_storage: The bucket must allow write, read and delete, and must not be public.
help.worker: Start the background worker; no heartbeat was seen in the last minute.
help.clock: The server clock differs from your browser's by more than 30 seconds; signatures and schedules depend on it.
help.secret_store: Set a real key-encryption key; placeholders are refused.

check.blocking: A blocking check failed, so setup cannot continue.
check.cannotContinue: Setup cannot continue until every blocking check passes.

node.title: Node identity
node.purpose: The installation's name, domain and jurisdiction, and its signing key.
node.name: Node name
node.jurisdictionHelp: The country whose law the node operator follows. Restricted places are never offered.
node.key: A signing key is generated when you continue. Only its public key and fingerprint are ever shown; the private key never is.

hub.title: Hub identity
hub.purpose: Configure your country or city without code: starting point, territory, name in every language, languages, currency and time zone.
hub.exampleNote: Example values are synthetic; replace them with yours.
hub.startHelp: A country pack brings regions, identifier formats, currency and legal facts; the generic profile brings ISO data only.
hub.territoryHelp: A country, region or place code, for example US-CA:san-diego.
hub.name: Hub name
hub.nameHelp: Required in every hub language; you can add the other languages in the console.
hub.languagesHelp: Language tags, the default first, for example en, es.

operator.title: Operator
operator.purpose: The legal entity that operates the hub, its contacts, its ownership declaration and its sanctions screening.
operator.ownership: I declare the operator's ownership truthfully.
operator.screening: Screening runs on the engine's baseline list. With the fake adapter the result is labelled “fake: not a real screening”; a potential match opens a review that the operator cannot close.

admin.title: First administrator
admin.purpose: The first staff member, with a mandatory second factor and recovery codes shown once.
admin.name: Name
admin.passwordHelp: In this demo the name, e-mail and password never leave this page.
admin.secondFactorHelp: A second factor is mandatory; setup cannot finish without it.
admin.recoveryCodes: Ten single-use recovery codes appear here once, after the second factor is enrolled. In this demo none are generated.
admin.stored: I have stored the recovery codes.
admin.reducedSod: With one staff member the hub runs in reduced separation of duties; two-person actions wait until a second staff member joins.

residency.title: Storage and residency
residency.purpose: Where personal data is stored and processed, and which privacy regime the notices follow.
residency.countryHelp: Database, object storage and backups should be located there.
residency.egress: By default no non-public data leaves the residency country and nothing non-public goes to an external model provider until you allow it.

providers.title: Providers
providers.purpose: Every capability starts on its fake adapter, so the hub can be explored without accounts or costs.
providers.liveLater: Live connections are never made here: they need a passing synthetic test, an egress decision and a second person.
providers.models: For language models you can later connect a provider directly or through OpenRouter, an optional router.
providers.invite: To invite the second staff member before e-mail is live, the console shows a one-time invitation link that expires in 72 hours.

modes.title: Modes
modes.purpose: How the hub starts: data mode, registration, modules, moderation and automation.
modes.defaults: Registration starts closed, every automation domain manual, indexing off; publications, magazine, events, search and communications are on. Change them later in the console.

review.title: Review
review.purpose: A summary of every step before you finish. Finishing records the configuration, creates the launch gates and invalidates the setup token.
review.afterFinish: After finishing, the hub is a draft: registration closed, every provider fake, indexing off.
